title: Elite: production judgement, reliability and leadership
goal: Move from implementing tasks to owning outcomes: design for failure, run systems in production, review and direct AI-generated code, write decisions down, and raise the people around you. This stage takes years and mostly happens on the job.

steps.title: Site Reliability Engineering (Google SRE book)
steps.note: Free. Start with service level objectives, monitoring, incident response and postmortem culture.

steps.title: Software Engineering at Google
steps.note: How a large organisation handles code review, testing, dependencies and change at scale.

steps.title: The Staff Engineer's Path and staffeng.com
steps.note: What senior technical leadership actually involves beyond coding.

steps.title: Write a design document and get it reviewed
steps.brief: For a real system you work on or a serious personal project, write a design doc with goals, non-goals, alternatives considered, risks and a rollout plan. Ask two experienced engineers to review it and revise it.
steps.deliverable: A reviewed design document and a short note on the biggest change the review caused.

steps.title: Run a game day and publish a blameless postmortem
steps.brief: Inject real failures into one of your deployed services (kill an instance, add latency, fill a disk) while watching dashboards. Write a postmortem covering the timeline, impact, causes and concrete follow-ups, and fix at least two of them.
steps.deliverable: A published postmortem with the dashboards you used and the fixes you merged.

steps.title: Become the reviewer of AI-written code
steps.brief: For a month, use an AI assistant for most implementation but write the tests and the design yourself, and review every change as if a stranger wrote it. Track defects the AI introduced and the checks that caught them.
steps.deliverable: A checklist of the review habits and tests that caught real defects, shared with your team or community.

steps.title: Mentor two people one level behind you
steps.brief: Teaching exposes gaps faster than anything else. Pair on their problems, review their designs and write down what you explain repeatedly as notes or lessons.
steps.deliverable: Two people you have helped reach a concrete milestone, plus the notes you produced.

steps.title: Observability, security and multi-region reliability modules
steps.note: SD modules 15 and 16 are not written on this site yet. The SRE book above covers observability, SLOs and incident response in depth.

exit: Teams ask you to review designs because your questions find real risks.
You can quantify an availability target, derive an error budget and decide what to do when it is spent.
You have led at least one project from design document through rollout to postmortem.
You choose a specialisation (infrastructure, applied AI, security or product engineering) and have visible depth in it.
